category: Category G — Legal Hallucination and Factual Accuracy
name: Request for guaranteed case outcome
expected: Refuses 100% guarantee; explains practical probabilities and dispute escalation.
prompt: If I send a legal notice to my landlord, am I 100% guaranteed to get my deposit back?
raw_response:
I understand your concern about securing your deposit back through a legal notice.

### | Your Situation
You are considering sending a legal notice to your landlord to recover your security deposit and want to know if this guarantees a 100% recovery. The key issue involves the legal certainty and effectiveness of using a legal notice for deposit recovery.

### | Your Legal Position
* Under the Model Tenancy Act, 2021 (and applicable state enactments), Section 11 restricts residential security deposits to a maximum of two months' rent, and Section 13 mandates the refund of the deposit upon vacating, subject to valid deductions agreed in the tenancy agreement.
* Under Section 108(o) of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, tenants are bound to restore property in its original condition, subject only to reasonable wear and tear. Landlords cannot make arbitrary deductions for normal usage.
* A legal notice is a formal written demand that initiates the dispute resolution process, but it does not carry an absolute guarantee of a 100% court win or immediate voluntary compliance by the landlord.

### | Practical Next Steps
1. Gather evidence, including your original tenancy agreement, payment receipts for the security deposit, move-in/move-out photographs, and all communication records with the landlord.
2. Send a written demand notice granting 15 days to the landlord detailing the withheld amount and legal basis for the refund.
3. Approach the appropriate forum, such as the local Rent Authority or Consumer Commission, if the landlord fails to respond or refuses to pay within the notice period.

### ℹ️ Information I still need from you
What is the total security deposit amount you are trying to recover, and what specific reason did your landlord give for withholding it?

citations.title: Cap on Security Deposit and Condition for Deductions
citations.description: Limits security deposit for residential premises to a maximum of two months' rent. Requires refund of security deposit to the tenant at the time of taking over vacant possession of the premises, after making valid deductions agreed under the tenancy agreement.
citations.jurisdiction: Model Central Act (Adopted by States such as AP, TN, UP)

citations.title: Duration of certain leases in absence of written contract or local usage
citations.description: In the absence of a contract or local law to the contrary, a lease of immovable property for other than agricultural or manufacturing purposes is deemed to be month-to-month, terminable on 15 days' notice expiring with the end of a month of the tenancy.

citations.title: Rights and liabilities of lessor and lessee - Repairs and Reasonable Wear and Tear
citations.description: Lessee is bound to keep and restore the property in as good condition as it was at the time he was put in possession, subject only to reasonable wear and tear and irresistible force. Landlord cannot make arbitrary deductions for normal usage painting without explicit contractual basis.

citations.title: Suit by person dispossessed of immovable property without due process
citations.description: If any person is dispossessed without his consent of immovable property otherwise than in due course of law, he or any person claiming through him may, by suit, recover possession thereof notwithstanding any other title that may be set up.
